thread:
maya: Quick design question — continuing the stream-conductor convo: do we prioritise soft end-to-end deadlines per-tenant or aggressively pack for GPU efficiency and accept occasional misses? need a simple deterministic tie-breaker so we can reason about regressions.

rajesh: My gut: hybrid. admit requests into short admission windows (e.g. 2–10ms) for packing, then within a window sort by slack = (deadline_ms - now - est_tail). if slack < expedite_threshold -> push to fast-path. else batch normally for packing.

maya: sounds plausible. how do we get est_tail cheaply?

rajesh: use per-route EWMA latency + token-count heuristic. cheap and adapts. pseudo: `slack = req.deadline - now - ewma(route) - tokens*per_token_ms`

olga: watch out for KV cache pressure when we expedite lots of short requests — we can end up evicting hot prefixes and increasing long requests' latency. need a preemption budget or cap on expedited concurrency.

rajesh: +1. add `expedite_budget_per_gpu` and decrement on fast-path dispatch. budget replenishes on successful batch completion.

Taylor: how does this interact with tiered SLAs? enterprise customers shouldn't be punted to packing.

rajesh: include tenant_weight in slack calc: `effective_slack = slack / tenant_weight` where lower weight means higher priority. weights come from billing/SLA mapping.

devon: operator surface: we should expose `admission_window_ms`, `expedite_threshold_ms`, `expedite_budget`, and `tenant_weight` per-namespace. Also a packing_hint boolean so some routes can force pack-only.

olga: Also emit metrics: `expedited_count`, `expedite_rejects_due_to_budget`, `kv_evictions_from_expedite`, `median_tail_by_path` so we can correlate.

maya: ok but still worried about oscillation: if we keep expediting, we reduce packing efficiency -> higher overall latency -> more expediting. we need damping.

rajesh: add a hysteresis factor: when packing efficiency (tokens/sec or GPU_util) drops below X, backoff expedite_rate by multiplicative factor until recovery.

devon: can we run controlled experiment? feature flag the expedite path and gate by sample percentage + tenant-tier whitelist. easy to measure delta in p99 and token-cost.

deploy-bot: conductor/stream-scheduler:deploy v2 -> staging succeeded :white_check_mark:

Taylor: nice. one more edge: long multi-turn chat requests where early tokens are cheap but later tokens blow up KV misses. slack calc needs to be token-position aware (e.g., predicted remaining tokens distribution).

rajesh: agreed — add `remaining_token_quantile` estimate from model stats. for now use conservative fallback (higher est_tail) for long sessions.

olga: implement quick guardrail: if expedite causes even one large eviction spike, auto-disable expedite for that tenant for 30s. simple and effective.

maya: this is great. can someone capture this as a short RFC: problem, hybrid algorithm, config knobs, metrics, experiment plan, safety guardrails (budget/hysteresis/auto-disable)? i'll drive reviews.

rajesh: I can draft baseline RFC today.

devon: i'll add operator API and rollout plan.

olga: i'll add KV observability hooks and eviction alerts.

Taylor: i'll own the experiment dashboard queries.

maya: awesome. thanks team :thumbsup:
